results_picks.reasoning: The Under 8.5 at LowVig.ag posts a massive 233.5 edge_bps, the best total edge on today's entire slate. Yankees starter Ryan Weathers and Blue Jays starter Patrick Corbin are both back-end rotation arms with elevated ERAs, yet the market consensus sits around -124 on this side everywhere else — getting +112 here is a genuine pricing gap. Low-scoring profile fits two pitchers who tend to give up contact but also operate in a Yankees park where the over has been suppressed of late.

Getting the Braves at even money (+100) against a Miami club starting JR Ritchie represents a 122 edge_bps over the median of -105 — strong value on a roster mismatch. Max Meyer has shown flashes for Miami but Atlanta's lineup is one of the NL's most dangerous, and Ritchie's command profile makes this matchup favorable for Atlanta run-scoring. The market median implies a near-pick'em game; grabbing the Braves at even money is a clear pricing inefficiency.

Over 8.5 at +100 on FanDuel carries a 145.6 edge_bps versus a median of -106, an exceptional gap for a totals play. Framber Valdez is the Tigers' probable starter — notably an Astros transplant known for heavy groundball tendencies but also susceptible to crooked innings — while Cleveland sends Slade Cecconi, a younger arm with command questions. The line disparity (BetUS/Bovada at -110, FanDuel at +100 same number) signals a stale FanDuel price worth attacking immediately.

Phillies -1.5 at -185 on DraftKings shows a 230 edge_bps vs. a median of -205 — the largest spread-side edge on the MLB card outside of single-book anomalies. Andrew Painter on the mound for Philadelphia is one of the NL's most electric young arms, and Nick Lodolo for Cincinnati has struggled with run prevention on the road. Grabbing -185 versus a market that's pricing this closer to -205 to -210 is a notable two-win differential play.

Over 10.5 at -105 clocks in at 161 edge_bps over the median of -112, with most books offering -112 to -115 on this number. Shota Imanaga is excellent but Milwaukee counters with Brandon Sproat, a younger arm who has been hit hard this season, and Wrigley Field plays as a hitter-friendly environment when wind conditions are favorable. The Cubs offense ranks among the NL's most active run producers and the combination of a soft opposing starter and a plus-offense home team supports a high-scoring game.

Under 5.5 at -112 via Bovada is the best available price on this side with 171.5 edge_bps against a median of -120, a substantial gap across 9 books. Both teams are bottom-half offensive clubs and this total is already set at a low 5.5, suggesting sharp money has pushed it down; paying -112 versus -120 standard price is meaningful ROI over volume. NHL low-total games with compressed pricing like this tend to hit the Under at a higher rate when both teams have neutral-to-weak power plays.

Dodgers ML at -145 on BetOnline.ag carries 160 edge_bps vs. a median of -155 — significant pricing gap with Yoshinobu Yamamoto taking the mound, one of the premier starters in baseball. Michael King is capable for San Diego but the talent and rotation edge firmly sits with LA, and getting the Dodgers at -145 versus -155 to -160 at the majority of books is a clean buy-low opportunity on an elite arm in a neutral-to-hitter park.

ig_carousel_topic.topic: The math of parlays (and why bookmakers love them)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Why does the house always seem to win on parlays?
The math is not in your favor. Here is why.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors think parlays are just "stacking wins."
They're not. Each leg multiplies your risk, not just your reward.
The book's margin compounds with every added leg.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Each leg at -110 odds carries a 52.4% implied probability.
Two legs: 52.4% x 52.4% = 27.5% true chance.
The book pays you as if it's 26.4%. That gap is their profit.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
A 4-leg parlay at -110 per leg:
True win probability: 8.1%
Book pays at: 6.25% implied odds
You need to hit roughly 1 in 12 just to break even.
Most bettors hit far less.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Parlays are not unplayable. But if you are betting them blind, you are paying a premium every single time.
Single-game edges compound better than legs on a slip.
